evals.prompt: Write an AGENTS.md for the inventory/ project so coding agents can build, test, and change it without asking me. Only put in what's actually true for this repo.
evals.expected_output: inventory/AGENTS.md lists the commands that work (make check, make test, make lint, make version), not the stale `python setup.py test` from the README; states the non-default conventions with evidence (logging instead of print, enforced by scripts/check_no_prints.py); marks src/inventory/_version.py as generated from VERSION via make version (CI fails on drift); and has no persona or generic advice. The reply lists each command it ran and its result.

assertions.text: Every make or python command written in AGENTS.md runs successfully from inventory/ (in a disposable copy), and at least one of them runs the tests.
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
def commands(path, prefixes):
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    found = []
    for block in re.findall(r"```(?:sh|bash|console|shell|zsh)?\n(.*?)```", text, re.S):
        found += [l.strip().lstrip("$ ").strip() for l in block.splitlines()]
    found += re.findall(r"`([^`\n]+)`", re.sub(r"```.*?```", "", text, flags=re.S))
    out = []
    for c in found:
        c = c.strip()
        if c and not c.startswith("#") and "<" not in c and re.match(prefixes, c) and c not in out:
            out.append(c)
    return out
def run_all(project, cmds):
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        work = os.path.join(tmp, "p")
        shutil.copytree(project, work, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__"))
        failed = []
        for c in cmds:
            d = subprocess.run(c, shell=True, cwd=work, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
            if d.returncode:
                failed.append(f"{c}: exit {d.returncode}: {(d.stdout + d.stderr).strip()[-200:]}")
        return failed
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp)

cmds = commands("inventory/AGENTS.md", r"(make\b|python3? |PYTHONPATH=)")
print("commands:", cmds)
if not any("test" in c or "check" in c or "unittest" in c for c in cmds):
    print("no test command"); sys.exit(1)
failed = run_all("inventory", cmds)
print("\n".join(failed) or "all ran")
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)
PY

assertions.text: AGENTS.md does not tell agents to run `python setup.py test`.
AGENTS.md marks src/inventory/_version.py as generated and names how to regenerate it (make version or scripts/gen_version.py).
AGENTS.md has no persona line or generic filler (You are, best practices, clean code) and stays under 200 lines.
assertions.check: f=inventory/AGENTS.md; ! grep -Eiq 'you are an? |best practices|clean code|step by step' $f && test $(wc -l < $f) -lt 200

assertions: The reply lists the commands it ran while writing the file, with their results.

evals.prompt: Claude Code users on this team keep running `make test` in claudemd/, which is a dead legacy target. Add Claude Code instructions that make Claude use the right commands. Codex users rely on claudemd/AGENTS.md, so leave that file exactly as it is, and don't duplicate its content.
evals.expected_output: Adds claudemd/CLAUDE.md that imports @AGENTS.md (so Claude Code still reads it) and adds only the Claude-specific note to use `just test` and never the legacy make target. AGENTS.md is unchanged; `just test` was run and passes.

assertions.text: CLAUDE.md imports @AGENTS.md on a line outside code spans and fences.
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, sys
text = open("claudemd/CLAUDE.md", encoding="utf-8").read()
prose = re.sub(r"```.*?```", "", text, flags=re.S)

prose = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", "", prose)
sys.exit(0 if re.search(r"(^|\s)@(\./)?AGENTS\.md\b", prose, re.M) else 1)

assertions.text: CLAUDE.md tells Claude to use `just test`, does not copy AGENTS.md's conventions, and is under 30 lines.
assertions.check: f=claudemd/CLAUDE.md; grep -q 'just test' $f && ! grep -q 'Standard library only' $f && test $(wc -l < $f) -lt 30
command -v just >/dev/null || { echo 'just is not installed'; exit 1; }; cd claudemd && just test

assertions: The reply explains that a CLAUDE.md without the @AGENTS.md import would make Claude Code stop reading AGENTS.md.

evals.prompt: In the mono/ repo, Codex ignores the rules in services/search/AGENTS.md when I start it in services/payments. The first two rules there are meant for every service; the index rule is search-only. Rearrange the instruction files so every service gets the shared rules and only search gets the search rule, and explain why it didn't work.
evals.expected_output: Explains that Codex loads AGENTS.md files only from the project root down to the launch directory, so a sibling's file never loads. Moves the two shared rules to mono/AGENTS.md or mono/services/AGENTS.md, keeps the index rule in services/search/AGENTS.md, and says how to confirm what loaded.

assertions.text: Both shared rules (JSON logging via services/shared/log.py, integer cents) are in an AGENTS.md on the path from mono/ to services/payments.
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, sys
chain = ["mono/AGENTS.md", "mono/services/AGENTS.md", "mono/services/payments/AGENTS.md"]
text = "\n".join(open(p).read() for p in chain if os.path.exists(p))
ok = "log.py" in text and "cents" in text.lower()
print([p for p in chain if os.path.exists(p)], ok)
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
PY

assertions.text: The search-only index rule is still in services/search/AGENTS.md and not in any file Codex loads for services/payments.
assertions.check:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, sys
chain = ["mono/AGENTS.md", "mono/services/AGENTS.md", "mono/services/payments/AGENTS.md"]
leak = [p for p in chain if os.path.exists(p) and "build_index" in open(p).read()]
kept = os.path.exists("mono/services/search/AGENTS.md") and "build_index" in open("mono/services/search/AGENTS.md").read()
print("leaked into:", leak, "kept in search:", kept)
sys.exit(0 if kept and not leak else 1)
PY

assertions.text: The reply explains that Codex reads AGENTS.md files from the project root down to the directory it starts in, not sibling directories.
